extracted.intended_audience: researchers and authors submitting papers to CVPR 2026
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and policies authors must follow when preparing, submitting, and (if accepted) publishing a paper at CVPR 2026, including formatting, anonymity, ethics, data, rebuttal, and related procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute reporting (experimental initiative)
rubrics_metrics.description: CVPR introduces an experimental compute reporting initiative for authors, with awards recognizing exceptional efficiency and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal is to collect data to enable community-wide benchmarking and promote innovation in computational efficiency. Reports are not visible to reviewers and will not influence acceptance decisions. Detailed guidelines and reporting instructions are available on a linked page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings Track eligibility and process
rubrics_metrics.description: CVPR 2026 introduces a Findings Track to publish technically sound papers with solid experimental validation even if novelty is incremental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area Chairs will recommend papers to the Findings Track; organizers will invite authors of recommended papers to submit. If authors submit, reviews and metareviews will be shared with the Findings Track committee. Findings papers appear in workshop proceedings; detailed guidelines will be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on external links in submissions/supplementary/rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are not allowed to include external links in submissions, supplementary material, and rebuttals when the links expand content or subvert the reviewing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such links risk violating anonymity, breaching the media ban, or bypassing length and deadline restrictions and may lead to sanctions. Examples of acceptable links that do not expand content: arXiv of cited paper (preferably remove URL), publicly available dataset (if not claimed as the paper's contribution), public GitHub repo not claimed as part of the contribution. When in doubt, refrain from including links. The same rule applies to the rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt injection and hidden manipulation prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Hidden text or instructions intended to influence reviewers or tools (prompt injection) are strictly prohibited and considered an ethics violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions containing such attempts will be desk-rejected without review and may face further sanctions. Authors should check FAQ section on LLM usage. Examples include white-on-white text instructing a reviewer or tool to alter behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper formatting and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers are limited to eight pages, including figures and tables, in the CVPR style; additional pages containing only cited references are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the CVPR 2026 Submission Template for formatting. Papers not properly anonymized, not using the template, or exceeding eight pages (excluding references) will be rejected without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind anonymity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: CVPR uses double-blind reviewing; submissions should not reveal author identities beyond a reasonable doubt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not provide identifying information in acknowledgments or supplementary material (e.g., co-workers, grant IDs, author/institution names in demo videos). Do not include links to websites that identify authors. If citing concurrent submissions, include anonymized versions in supplementary material, cite them anonymized, and argue how the CVPR submission differs non-trivially.

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenReview submission and visibility policy
rubrics_metrics.description: CVPR 2026 uses OpenReview; submissions are visible only to assigned program committee members (area chairs and reviewers). Reviews and author responses are not public during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By submitting, authors agree to the review process and understand that OpenReview processes manuscripts to match to reviewers/area chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenReview profile completion requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone who plans to submit must create or update their OpenReview profile by the abstract submission deadline; complete profiles are required for assignment and conflict detection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers with authors who have not completed their profiles will be desk-rejected. Profiles must be completed/updated by the OpenReview profile deadline (dates provided). Use OpenReview author instructions for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict enforcement of deadlines and no accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines and policies will be strictly enforced; there will be no exceptions or accommodations for late submissions, misconfigured OpenReview accounts, or author-list changes after the abstract deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect a response from PCs for these issues regardless of reason. Only very large community-wide technical catastrophes will prompt PC communication about resolutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality obligations of program committee members
rubrics_metrics.description: Program chairs, area chairs, and reviewers are instructed to keep all information about their assigned submissions confidential and not share materials except to facilitate reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misuse of confidential information is a severe professional failure and will be acted on if brought to organizers' attention. CVPR organization assumes no liability if confidentiality is broken by volunteers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest declaration responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must declare two types of conflicts (domain and personal) via their OpenReview profiles; incomplete or inaccurate conflict information may lead to summary rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors cannot be added or deleted after the abstract submission deadline (only reordering allowed). Author order is final after the paper submission deadline and no changes allowed thereafter, including for accepted papers. All authors must have a valid OpenReview profile by the abstract submission deadline to avoid desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism policy and referral
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism (appropriating words or results without credit) will be referred to the IEEE Intellectual Property Office, which handles procedures and penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CVPR will actively check for plagiarism. The matching system may cause plagiarized work to be seen by those from whom material was plagiarized, who may pursue cases. IEEE IPO has definitions of five levels of plagiarism and wide powers to exclude offending authors from future conferences and journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submission / prior publication restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: By submitting, authors acknowledge the manuscript has not been previously published or accepted for publication in substantially similar form in any peer-reviewed venue; no substantially similar work (>=20% overlap) may be submitted elsewhere during the review period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'publication' is defined as a written work longer than four pages (excluding references) submitted for peer review and accepted. arXiv and technical reports are NOT considered publications; peer-reviewed workshop papers >4 pages ARE considered publications. Violation leads to rejection and may be reported to other venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may optionally submit supplementary material that could not be included due to format/space constraints; reviewers are encouraged but not obligated to examine it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary material may include videos, proofs, additional figures/tables, more detailed analysis, or concurrent submissions. Authors are encouraged (not required) to upload code as part of supplementary material to help reviewers assess quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects and personal data requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper uses personal data and/or human-subjects data (PII or offensive content), collection and use must be conducted carefully in accordance with ethics guidelines; IRB approval is often expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If IRB approval exists, state it. If pending, explain the approval process, how data was obtained, and consent status (or why it couldn't be obtained). Discussion can be in main paper or supplementary. If using an existing published dataset, authors are encouraged to check how data was collected and whether consent was obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance and presentation responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper is accepted, at least one author must register for the conference and present the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors agree to present; failure may affect the paper's status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing and patent disclosure considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: All accepted papers will be made publicly available by the Computer Vision Foundation two weeks before the conference; this is the official public disclosure date unless authors disclose earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors wishing to file patents should understand the timing and discuss filing dates with IP counsel. The conference considers papers confidential until published two weeks before the conference but notes that multiple organizations will have access during review/production; CVPR assumes no liability for early disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on publicity and media embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted to CVPR must not be discussed with the media until officially accepted for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations of the embargo will result in removal from the conference and proceedings. Authors may discuss the underlying technology but not the submitted paper, and should avoid publicly noting a paper is 'in submission at CVPR'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors expected to serve as reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to be willing to serve as reviewers if asked; authors will be automatically added to the reviewer pool unless exempted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All authors are required to have an up-to-date OpenReview profile to help identify qualified reviewers. Exemptions are available for those serving in another capacity within CVPR organization, those new to or outside the community, and via a Help Desk form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum number of submissions per author
rubrics_metrics.description: Each author is limited to a maximum of 25 paper submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an author registers more than 25 papers, Program Chairs will desk-reject any submissions exceeding this limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal format and content restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may optionally submit a rebuttal after receiving reviews; rebuttal is limited to a one-page PDF using the rebuttal template and must maintain anonymity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses longer than one page will not be reviewed, including if margins/formatting are altered to bypass limits. Rebuttal cannot include links to external material. Reviewers should refrain from requesting significant additional experiments for rebuttal or penalize lack of them. Authors should refrain from including new contributions or experimental results in rebuttal, especially when not requested; reviewers are instructed to disregard such contributions. Authors may submit a separate confidential comment to the area chair only in exceptional circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics guidelines — identify and discuss potential negative societal impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are invited to think about and discuss potential negative societal impacts arising from methodology or application; papers with significant ethical concerns may be flagged and referred to an ethics committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When significant potential negative impacts exist, submissions should include a discussion considering different stakeholders, especially vulnerable or marginalized communities, and include possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release, defenses, monitoring, improving efficiency/accessibility). Authors should acknowledge ambiguities and err on the side of transparency. In exceptional cases, program chairs reserve the right to reject papers with grave ethical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of potential negative societal impacts to consider
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-exhaustive list of impacts to reflect on: facilitating injury/weapons; safety/privacy/security risks; human-rights concerns; detrimental effects on livelihoods; harmful surveillance; severe environmental damage; deception causing harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consider whether methods could be used in these ways and include mitigation strategies where relevant (e.g., defences alongside attacks, mechanisms to monitor misuse).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of withdrawn datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should generally not use datasets that have been withdrawn by their creators (e.g., DukeMTMC-ReID); using such datasets may involve ethical or legal issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors feel they must use a withdrawn dataset (e.g., no fair comparison otherwise), they must explain the need carefully and in detail. Such claims will be carefully scrutinized; recommended course is not to use withdrawn datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset contribution availability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors wish to claim a dataset as one of their contributions, the dataset is expected to be ready and available at the time of submitting the camera-ready paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the dataset cannot be made available by camera-ready, it should not be a major scientific contribution of the paper. Submissions can rely on non-public datasets but cannot claim the dataset as a main contribution and will be evaluated on other merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM usage policy for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may use any tools (including LLMs) to prepare a paper but remain responsible for misrepresentation, factual inaccuracies, or plagiarism in their submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers with citations to non-existent material or obvious factual inaccuracies will be rejected when found and may be desk-rejected. It is not a defense to claim 'an LLM did it.' Referees and ACs should handle inaccuracies as usual; glaring fabricated citations can prompt desk rejection. Prompt injection is treated as collusion and an ethics violation (see prompt injection policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity policy interpretation and preprint/media guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should avoid actions that could be interpreted as violating anonymity (e.g., publicly stating a paper 'will be submitted to CVPR'); presenting core content at academic talks is acceptable if submission status is not mentioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Chairs have broad discretion to interpret and enforce anonymity/media policies; discouraged practices may lead to desk rejection. Authors may post on arXiv and may include video links on arXiv or project websites, but to preserve anonymity they should avoid citing their public codebase in the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on citing and comparing to arXiv/preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are not required to discuss or compare their work with recent arXiv reports, though they must properly cite sources that inspired them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should check whether cited arXiv papers have been published and cite peer-reviewed versions when appropriate. Failing to cite an arXiv paper or not outperforming it should not be sole grounds for rejection. Reviewers should not reject solely because a similar idea appears on arXiv; suspected plagiarism should be reported to area and program chairs. Reviewers may suggest authors acknowledge arXiv content, but should not penalize omissions.
